sentence_stem: Had the committee been informed earlier,
correct_completion: the project would have been approved last month.
full_sentence: Had the committee been informed earlier, the project would have been approved last month.
acceptable_variants: the budget would have been secured.
the decision would have been different.

options.text: the project would be approved now.
options.why_wrong: The stem describes a past condition ('had been informed earlier'), so the result must also refer to the past, not the present.

options.text: the project was approved last month.
options.why_wrong: Without 'would have', this is a simple statement of fact and does not complete the hypothetical result of the inverted condition.

options.text: the project would have been approved last month.
the project would have approved last month.
options.why_wrong: After 'would have' the verb must be a past participle in the passive, 'been approved'; 'approved' alone is incorrect.

explanation: Inversion replaces 'if' by moving 'had' to the front of the clause, so the stem still expresses a past condition. The main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle. Learners often keep the full 'if' form or drop the auxiliary, because Portuguese speakers may not expect inverted conditionals in formal English.
translation: Se o comitê tivesse sido informado mais cedo, o projeto teria sido aprovado no mês passado.
